question: What does WHO recommend regarding bupropion for smoking cessation, and what serious adverse events (SAEs) and dropout risk does the WHO guideline document for bupropion compared to other cessation medications?
expected_answer: WHO recommends bupropion as a first-line pharmacological treatment for tobacco users who smoke. The balance of benefits against harms favours bupropion on the basis of large benefits (NNT: 14 vs placebo) and moderate harms: SAEs included anxiety, insomnia and psychiatric AEs (NNH: 100 to cause one additional SAE), and dropouts due to adverse events (NNH: 33). Discontinuation of therapy due to adverse events may also be more common with bupropion than other cessation monotherapies.
required_claims: Bupropion is recommended as a first-line pharmacotherapy for smoking cessation
Bupropion SAEs include anxiety, insomnia, and psychiatric AEs with NNH of 100
Dropout rate due to adverse events for bupropion has NNH of 33

required_metrics.outcome: serious adverse events (anxiety, insomnia, psychiatric AEs)
